extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants and their accountants / legal advisors preparing SEC Form 8-K and related registration/proxy filings for business acquisitions
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and interpretive guidance governing which financial statements of an acquired business must be prepared and filed on Form 8-K (or Form 8-K/A), the required periods and age of those statements, timing (including the 71-day amendment period), significance thresholds, and interactions with registration statements and proxy filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 9.01(a) — Financial statements of acquired businesses or funds
rubrics_metrics.description: For any business acquisition or fund acquisition required to be described in answer to Item 2.01 of this form, file financial statements and any applicable supplemental information of the business acquired specified in Rules 3-05 or 3-14 of Regulation S-X, or Rules 8-04 or 8-06 of Regulation S-X for smaller reporting companies, or of the fund acquired specified in Rule 6-11 of Regulation S-X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirement applies when the acquisition must be described under Item 2.01. See Rules 3-05/3-14 (or 8-04/8-06 for smaller reporting companies) and Rule 6-11 for funds for the specific financial statement content and supplemental information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and preparation requirements (Regulation S-X compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The financial statements must be prepared pursuant to Regulation S-X; supporting schedules need not be filed unless required by Rule 6-11. A manually signed accountant’s report should be provided pursuant to Rule 2-02 of Regulation S-X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial statements required by Item 9.01 must comply with Reg S-X technical requirements; include accountant's report as required. For funds or special cases, supporting schedules may be required under specific rules (e.g., Rule 6-11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing — Initial filing vs. 71-day amendment window
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements required by this item may be filed with the initial report, or by amendment not later than 71 calendar days after the date that the initial report on Form 8-K must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not included in the initial report, the registrant should indicate this in the Form 8-K and state when required financial statements will be filed. The registrant may, at its option, include unaudited financial statements in the initial Form 8-K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of 'age' of required financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The age of the financial statements of an acquired business to be included in a Form 8-K is determined by reference to the earlier of (a) the date the Form 8-K is initially filed; or (b) the due date of the Form 8-K reporting the acquisition (four business days after the transaction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing date of the initial Form 8-K or its due date is used to determine how current the Rule 3-05 financial statements must be; filing the amendment within the 71-day extension does not change the required age (except as affected by a registration statement effective date—see separate criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8-K filing deadline for reporting acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Form 8-K reporting the acquisition must be filed on or before the fourth business day following the date of the acquisition’s consummation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This four-business-day deadline is the baseline for computing required statement age and for invoking the 71-day amendment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant type and applicable S-X rules for required statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Which specific S-X rules apply depends on the registrant: registrants that are SRCs follow Rule 8-02 (annual) and Rule 8-03 (interim); all other registrants use Rule 3-01 (balance sheet), Rule 3-02 (income statement and cash flows), Rule 3-04 (statement of changes in stockholders’ equity), and Rule 3-05 for acquired businesses; funds use Rule 6-11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine registrant category (SRC, accelerated filer, large accelerated, non-accelerated) to identify the exact S-X rules and formatting requirements applicable to the acquired business financials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required periods and number of years depends on significance of acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of periods required is determined based on the significance of the acquired business: if significance is 20% or less — none; exceeds 20% but not 40% — most recent fiscal year (and unaudited subsequent interim financial statements) with no comparative interim period; greater than 40% — audited financial statements for the most recent fiscal year and the prior year, plus unaudited subsequent interim statements and comparative interim statements of the prior year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the acquired business is a real estate operation subject to Rule 3-14 and significance is >20% but ≤40%, the requirement is similar to the middle tier (most recent fiscal year plus subsequent interim statements) without comparative interim financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim-period requirements vary with timing of Form 8-K filing (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific interim periods required (e.g., three months, six months, nine months) depend on the date the initial Form 8-K is filed relative to the acquired business’s fiscal quarter-ends and the registrant/target filer status (accelerated filer vs non-accelerated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show that filing before/after key cutoff dates (e.g., 135 days after quarter-end) changes whether three-month or six-month interim statements are required; accelerated filer status of the acquired business also affects which interim periods must be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: 71-day extension does not change required age of financial statements (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The age of financial statements that must be included in the Form 8-K is not affected by the 71-day automatic extension of time to file the financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of the 71-day extension does not require filing more current statements on Form 8-K unless other events (e.g., registration statement effectiveness during the extension) change the applicable date for determining age.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of registration statement becoming effective during the 71-day extension
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registration statement becomes effective during the 71-day extension period, the age of Rule 3-05 financial statements filed on Form 8-K/A is based on the effective date of the registration statement (or mailing date of the proxy) rather than the initial Form 8-K filing date, provided the acquisition is less than 50% significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S-X Rule 3-05(b)(4) allows omission from a registration/proxy if effective during the extension (not more than 74 days after consummation) unless acquisition is 50% or more significant; however, even if omitted from the registration statement, the financial statements still must be included in the Form 8-K within its timeframe and their age is measured from the registration effective date when that effective date falls within the extension period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously filed financial statements may satisfy Form 8-K if 'substantially the same'
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant previously has reported substantially the same information as required by Form 8-K, the registrant need not make an additional report; disclosures about previously reported events may be provided by incorporation by reference to the previously filed report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEC staff guidance: audited annual financial statements are not substantially the same as unaudited interim financial statements; interim statements prepared as of a date more than one quarter different from the required 'as of' date are not substantially the same and must be updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-X Rule 3-12 — Age of financial statements for registration/proxy filings (update requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the financial statements in a filing are as of a date the number of days specified in paragraph (g) (130 days for large accelerated/accelerated filers; 135 days for others) or more before the anticipated effective date/mailing date, the financial statements shall be updated with an interim balance sheet within that number of days and with interim statements of comprehensive income and cash flows for the interim period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (b) permits, when the anticipated effective date falls within the number of days subsequent to fiscal year-end specified in (g), inclusion of financials only as current as of the third fiscal quarter unless audited year-end statements are available. Paragraph (c) requires audited year-end statements to be included if they become available prior to effectiveness. See specific day thresholds in paragraph (g).

rubrics_metrics.name: S-X Rule 8-08 — Age of financial statements for non-Form 10-K filings
rubrics_metrics.description: At the date of filing, financial statements included in filings other than filings on Form 10-K must be not less current than the financial statements that would be required in Forms 10-K and 10-Q; if required financial statements are as of a date 135 days or more before the effective or expected mailing date, they must be updated to include interim financial statements ending within 135 days of the effective or expected mailing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim financial statements may be unaudited and need not be in greater detail than required by Rule 10-01; when anticipated effective or mailing date falls within 45 days after fiscal year-end, the filing may include statements current only to the end of the third fiscal quarter unless audited year-end statements are available and must be included if available.
